_about: What each shipped episode already used. The creative gate (tools/creative_gate.py) refuses a new episode whose META['creative'] repeats any of these. Append an episode here when its master is approved.

episodes.title: We Let a Black Hole Loose in Our Solar System
episodes.story_shape: intruder approach: something invisible drifts in over years, we watch it disrupt the planets, then branch into endings
episodes.point_of_view: god's-eye orbital view of the Solar System with a narrator addressing you
episodes.narrator: second person: you, watching from home
episodes.hook_device: a countdown: years left until it arrives
episodes.ending_device: three endings for Earth (falls in, scorched, frozen) then the odds: should you worry
episodes.thumb_device: big headline number over the scene: 30 YEARS LEFT
episodes.palette: black space with hot orange accretion glow
episodes.signature_shot: the black hole's lensing ring sliding past the planets

episodes.title: We Dropped a Ship Into Jupiter. Here's How Far It Got.
episodes.story_shape: descent: one object falls layer by layer with a depth and time counter until it fails
episodes.narrator: second person: you, inside the ship
episodes.hook_device: how far does it get before something stops it
episodes.time_scale: minutes to hours of a single fall
episodes.ending_device: the ship is lost; we keep going without you to the core
episodes.thumb_device: big headline text over the scene: STILL NO GROUND
episodes.palette: amber, brown and cream Jupiter cloud bands
episodes.signature_shot: dropping through the cloud decks into the red glowing dark

episodes.title: A Rogue Planet Is Coming. The Date It Arrives Decides Everything.
episodes.story_shape: intruder approach rerun 730 times: the arrival date branches Earth into fates
episodes.point_of_view: from the ground on Earth looking up, plus orbital views of the simulation runs
episodes.narrator: second person: you, on the ground
episodes.hook_device: a date on the calendar decides everything
episodes.ending_device: four fates (scorched, frozen, thrown out, Moon lost) then the odds: should you worry
episodes.thumb_device: an everyday object (a wall calendar with one date circled) framing the cosmic event outside the window
episodes.palette: deep violet and ice blue night
episodes.signature_shot: a giant violet planet rising over a city by the bay

episodes.title: These Fish Saw the First Hour After the Dinosaur Asteroid. Here's Every Minute.
episodes.story_shape: one riverbank, one clock: a two-hour vigil 3,050 km from the impact, counted by what arrives, inside a forensic frame (fossil evidence at open and close)
episodes.point_of_view: eye level and underwater in a Cretaceous river (Tanis); no orbital Solar System views
episodes.hook_device: a lightning-count: flash first, sound last, and a paddlefish breathing in glass
episodes.time_scale: seconds to two and a half hours
episodes.ending_device: forensic close: glass in amber and in fossil gills matched to the crater, then the sound arriving last
episodes.thumb_device: from under the river: Snell's window full of shooting stars with a paddlefish crossing it
episodes.palette: fern green, river silt and ember red
episodes.signature_shot: glass beads raining from a clear sky into a river while a paddlefish feeds
